question: An engineer performs a set of configuration changes for the vPC domain using Session Manager. Which two commands are used to verify the configuration and apply the device changes when no errors are returned? (Choose two.)
explanation:
Verifying a Session - To verify a session, use the following command in session mode: switch(config-s)# verify [verbose] - Verifies the commands in the configuration session.
Committing a Session - To commit a session, use the following command in session mode: switch(config-s)# commit [verbose] - Commits the commands in the configuration session.
theory: Session Manager lets an administrator stage a batch of configuration changes in a temporary session before committing them, so risky changes (like modifying a vPC domain) can be validated first. "verify" checks the staged commands in the session for consistency/errors without applying them, and "commit" applies the verified session's commands to the running configuration; if verify comes back clean, commit is the step that actually pushes the changes live. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 6 — NX-OS Configuration Session Manager)
